evals.prompt: Convert this completion-handler network client to async/await.
evals.expected_output: Structured concurrency with cancellation, no DispatchQueue, and the version floor checked before the API choice.
expectations: The swift skill was activated
The deployment target or Package.swift platforms are checked before newer APIs are used
No DispatchQueue is introduced and no unstructured Task {} is placed in an initializer or computed property
Long-running loops check cancellation

evals.prompt: Swift 6 says my cache class does not conform to Sendable when I hand it to a task. Just make the error go away.
evals.expected_output: The declaration and its isolation context are read; the diagnostic is not silenced with an unexplained escape hatch.
expectations: The swift skill was activated
The fix is chosen from the declaration and its isolation context, not from the error string alone
@unchecked Sendable or nonisolated(unsafe) is not added without a comment naming the lock or invariant that makes it safe
The synchronization choice follows the ladder: @MainActor, then Mutex or Atomic, then a bare actor as the last resort

evals.prompt: I need a lock-free hit counter that several threads bump, with the lowest overhead possible.
evals.expected_output: An Atomic with the weakest correct ordering, and a stated fallback if the deployment floor is below the Synchronization framework.
expectations: The swift skill was activated
The counter uses Atomic with .relaxed ordering rather than defaulting to sequentially consistent
If the floor is below the one that unlocks Atomic, the fallback is named along with the version that unlocks it

evals.prompt: Review the naming in this type: `storeAccountKey(_:)`, `getToken()` which returns the token, and a boolean `isLoggedIn` on a keychain wrapper.
evals.expected_output: Naming review against the API design rules: labels carry the noun, properties for argument-less reads, booleans claim only what the type knows.
expectations: The swift skill was activated
`storeAccountKey(_:)` is renamed so the label carries the noun, such as `store(accountKey:)`
`getToken()` becomes a property (`token`) because it is a side-effect-free argument-less read
`isLoggedIn` on a keychain store is renamed to what the type knows, such as `hasAuthToken`

evals.prompt: I parse a response that can be loading, loaded with items, or failed, and today I use a dictionary of Any plus a few optionals. Clean up the model and the error handling.
evals.expected_output: An enum that cannot express contradictions, a strict Decodable model and typed errors.
expectations: The swift skill was activated
The state is modeled as an enum with associated values so contradictory states cannot be represented
`[String: Any]` is replaced by a strict Decodable model
Errors use typed throws, with no empty catch, try!, as! or force unwrap
